classification.difficultyReason: Infer equal interval sizes from labelled ticks and read indicated values, including a midpoint and fractional intervals.

content.prompt: Determine the value(s) the arrow is pointing to.

spec.description: Horizontal line with arrowheads at both ends and eleven equally spaced ticks. The sixth tick is labelled 0 above the line and the tenth is labelled 100. Upward arrows below the line indicate the fourth and ninth ticks.
spec.mathematics: Four intervals from 0 to 100 give 25 per interval. The indicated ticks are two intervals left of zero and three intervals right of zero.
spec.answerVisibility: Keep the supplied blue results out of the question diagram; retain them only in the answer fields.

spec.description: Horizontal line with arrowheads at both ends and eleven equally spaced downward ticks. The second tick is labelled −6 and the eleventh is labelled 3 below the line. A downward arrow indicates the midpoint between the fifth and sixth ticks.
spec.mathematics: Nine intervals from −6 to 3 give 1 per interval. The arrow is halfway between −3 and −2.
spec.answerVisibility: Keep the supplied blue −2.5 out of the question diagram; retain it only in the answer fields.

answer.worked:
There are nine equal intervals from $-6$ to $3$.
$$\begin{align*}
\text{Interval size}&=\frac{3-(-6)}{9}\\
&=1
\end{align*}$$
The arrow is halfway between $-3$ and $-2$, so its value is $-2.5$.

spec.description: Horizontal line without endpoint arrowheads, with twelve equally spaced ticks. The second tick is labelled −1 and the twelfth is labelled 1 below the line. The seventh tick is enclosed by an unfilled circle and has no number label. An upward arrow indicates the sixth tick.
spec.mathematics: Ten intervals from −1 to 1 give 0.2 per interval. The circled central tick represents zero, and the indicated tick immediately to its left represents −0.2.
spec.answerVisibility: Do not label the circled tick or indicated tick with their inferred values. The supplied blue decimal and fraction belong only in the answer fields.

answer.worked:
There are ten equal intervals from $-1$ to $1$.
$$\begin{align*}
\text{Interval size}&=\frac{1-(-1)}{10}\\
&=0.2
\end{align*}$$
The circled tick is zero. The arrow is one interval to its left, so its value is $-0.2=-\frac{1}{5}$.

spec.description: Shorter horizontal line without endpoint arrowheads, with eleven equally spaced downward ticks. The fourth tick is labelled −20 and the ninth is labelled −10 below the line. A downward arrow indicates the second tick.
spec.mathematics: Five intervals from −20 to −10 give 2 per interval. The arrow indicates two intervals left of −20.
spec.answerVisibility: Keep the supplied blue −24 out of the question diagram; retain it only in the answer fields.

answer.worked:
Each interval represents $10\div5=2$. The arrow is two intervals left of $-20$.
$$\begin{align*}
\text{Value}&=-20-2\times2\\
&=-24
\end{align*}$$
